new_findings.problem: The fixes add a sediment item to the path C audit: 'finished specs left in place, ... glossary terms of dropped work, research notes whose decision is recorded, archive folders'. Step 3 says 'Apply the approved items'. The skill never asks for the line-by-line pass before removing them, and never routes them to /harness:wrap. The template it installs allows the removal only that way: ':46 `/harness:wrap` proposes it' and ':53 once every line of its spec lives in a test, an ADR, the glossary or the commit message, the spec file goes'. Path B (:121-122) only lists the same items, so paths B and C disagree. The kit's own CHANGELOG [1.27.0] records that this kind of reduction failed without 'a line-by-line pass ... before anything is deleted'.
new_findings.scenario: An operator runs 'audit my Claude Code harness' on a long-lived repository that has 30 passing specs in specs/. They approve 'remove finished specs'. The session deletes the files. A non-goal or a 'for later' decision that lived only in one spec now has no home in the tree, so later sessions re-propose it. Git still has the file, but nothing points to it.
new_findings.fix: Path C step 3: run finished specs, research notes and dropped work's terms through `/harness:wrap`'s closures (the line-by-line pass, then propose and confirm), or list them as path B does and leave the removal to /harness:wrap.

new_findings.problem: The template closes a tracker ticket only under 'finished and reviewed: ... a spec or ticket in a tracker is closed there'. Wrap closes a ticket as soon as 'its acceptance tests pass', with no review gate. Build tells the operator to run wrap straight after the build, while the manual orders '/harness:check when the ticket is risky, then /harness:wrap'. Wrap also never says what 'closed as resolved' means for a kit-local ticket file under specs/<slug>/; deleting it would bypass the later line-by-line pass over 'any ticket files under specs/<slug>/'.
new_findings.scenario: A risky migration ticket is built, and build reminds the operator that wrap closes it. They run wrap, and the ticket is closed and its dependants unblocked before /harness:check has run. The next tickets build on unreviewed high-stakes code.
new_findings.fix: wrap:19: 'A ticket whose acceptance tests pass and whose review (if it needs one) is done: propose closing it'. Then say that a ticket file under specs/<slug>/ is marked resolved, not deleted, until its spec goes.

new_findings.problem: 'cited by path and commit' cannot be met on the default flow. /harness:task (task/SKILL.md:10-13) never commits, so at wrap step 1 the spec exists in no commit. Wrap commits the ADR and the spec together in step 6, and an ADR cannot contain the hash of the commit that adds it. Fixing the citation afterwards breaks the rule ':52 setting the old one's status is the only edit an accepted ADR takes'.
new_findings.scenario: The session cites `specs/refunds.md @ <HEAD>`, where HEAD is the pre-work commit in which the file does not exist. That wrong pointer then sits in a record nobody may edit.
new_findings.fix: Cite by path ('`git log --all -- <path>` finds it after removal'), or name the commit in the removal commit's message rather than in the ADR.

new_findings.problem: The N7 fix sends the operator's personal notes to `CLAUDE.local.md` but never says to gitignore it. First-party (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory): 'Add `CLAUDE.local.md` to your `.gitignore` so it isn't committed.' §8 records the run 'in the commit that carries it'. A committed CLAUDE.local.md loads for every teammate, because it is loaded wherever it exists in the tree.
new_findings.scenario: Path B moves the operator's personal memory notes into CLAUDE.local.md, and the setup commit includes it. Every teammate's session now loads one person's preferences.

grounds.verdict: accurate against the cited sources, with two caveats on the 55% basis and two leftover unnamed or stretched bases
notes: Nygard (cognitect 2011): 'If a decision is reversed, we will keep the old one around, but mark it as superseded.' Also 'If a later ADR changes or reverses a decision, it may be marked as "deprecated" or "superseded"'. README.md:228-229, README.ru.md and CHANGELOG.md:54-55 state this accurately. The rule 'only edit an accepted ADR takes' is the kit's own; Nygard does not address editing.

mattpocock: ADR-FORMAT.md:21 has optional Status '`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`', so 'the same statuses, plus `proposed`, as optional frontmatter' (README.md:229-230) is accurate. domain-modeling/SKILL.md:40 'Create files lazily: only when you have something to write' matches 'create these files only when there is something to write', where 'these files' means ADRs and the glossary. triage/OUT-OF-SCOPE.md:3 'persistent records of rejected feature requests' and :101-103 'Delete the `.out-of-scope/` file' match 'deleting the file when a rejection is reversed'. productivity/writing-for-agents/SKILL.md:80 'sediment: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky' is quoted accurately and now scoped 'for agent instructions'.

55% (README.md:227, README.ru.md:231): this matches the cited lab rule 0 verbatim ('55% коммитов только-`.md`'). Caveat 1: the primary record (devlog 0137, table) counts 'коммиты, трогающие только `.md`/`.json` — 759 из 1369 — 55%', i.e. Markdown or JSON, not only Markdown. Caveat 2: the record's headline is 'Документацию душил не дрейф, а стоимость её поддержки', and it lists 'Опровергнутая гипотеза: доки не устарели'. So the 55% measures upkeep cost, not unnoticed drift. In the README it directly follows 'drifts from the code unnoticed', a claim that comes from rule 0's reasoning, not from that measurement. 'to keep prose in step with code' is itself accurate. The same record calls the rule 'Формально это single-incident'.

Removing finished specs rests on the lab's rule 0 and on an analogy (writing-guide sediment). Mattpocock's own practice closes and keeps specs and tickets. 'The lab has not measured the effect on sessions' is stated, which is correct.

AGENTS.md:73-76, README.md:16-17 and CHANGELOG.md:59-61 agree on four bases. harness/SKILL.md:18-20 lists three, and gives 'established practice' as the basis for *How we work*, which none of that block's rationale cites (N11).

Still unnamed: the basis for `_Avoid_` (mattpocock GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md:27). README.md:237 says mattpocock keeps the glossary and ADRs 'instead' of auto memory, but mattpocock never mentions auto memory. README.ru.md drops 'instead'.

Auto memory first-party claims re-verified on code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: 'Auto memory is on by default in local sessions'; 'To turn it off for a single project, set `autoMemoryEnabled` in that project's settings'; the toggle 'saves `autoMemoryEnabled` to your user settings'.

EN/RU: README/README.ru and manual/manual.ru agree on every changed line. Both READMEs' command table (README.md:173, README.ru.md:174) still describes wrap as 'decisions into ADRs, terms into the glossary, evidence, commit' and omits that it now proposes deletions. This is an omission, not a contradiction.
